commands.short: the colours she answers in - a console of mood switches you can add, edit, rename, put away and put back
commands.desc: THE MOODS - THE COLOURS SHE ANSWERS IN (src/js/moods.js). A console of SWITCHES, not a single choice: a ROLE says who is on the stage, a TRAIT says what she is made of, and a MOOD says what KEY she is speaking in this hour. Every chip is a switch - switch on as many as you like (SLUTTY + BOSSY + SAVAGE), press one again to switch it off, ALL OFF is a chip too - and the colours that are on are COMBINED into ONE block of her own prompt, one rule after another, in the order they were switched on (and while every switch is off the block is NOT SENT AT ALL). It is the pencil's AI POLISH (src/js/draft.js) pointed the other way - a chip in front and the whole RULE behind it (the chip's tooltip, and /mood list) - and the PENCIL HAS THE SAME ROW: the colours in force are handed to the model with a rewrite too, so the STYLE decides the job and the MOODS decide the register it comes back in. THE LIST IS A FILE: the shipped moods are THE BOOK at src/moods/moods.json, a plain list of names and rules - add one there (or take one out) and /mood reload, or a page reload, makes it a switch, with no code touched. TWEAKING ONE IS DONE IN THE PANEL, NOT IN THE FILE: the MOOD panel's EDIT button (and the SYSTEM panel's MOOD row) opens THE MOOD EDITOR - pick any mood, shipped or written here, and write its NAME and its RULE; SAVE keeps it (a shipped mood's change lives on this device - the book is never written to), RESET puts a shipped mood's own wording back, PUT IT BACK returns one that was taken off the console, and RENAME never moves the mood's id, so every board that names it still finds it. THIS DOOR: bare or `state` prints what is in force; `<NAME>` FLIPS that switch; `<NAME> + <NAME>` flips several; `on <NAME>` / `off <NAME>` say which way; `off` alone switches everything off; `<NAME> :: <HOW SHE IS TO SOUND>` writes a NEW colour of your own (kept on this device) and switches it on - and the same line RE-SAYS A SHIPPED ONE, which is kept on this device too, so the book itself is never written to; `edit <NAME> :: <THE WORDS>` rewrites one, `rename <NAME> :: <NEW NAME>` changes the chip; `reset <NAME>` puts a shipped mood's own words back; `delete <NAME>` PUTS ONE AWAY, and NOTHING IS DESTROYED - the book and the device both still hold it; `restore <NAME>` puts it back on the console; `list` prints every mood with its rule, the ones put away included; `reload` re-reads the book. THE SYSTEM PANEL'S MOOD ROW AND THE PENCIL'S ROW ARE THIS SAME CONSOLE BY PRESS, with EDIT (THE MOOD EDITOR - the whole of CRUD with buttons), + NEW MOOD and DELETE in the panel. SHE HAS THE SAME LANE: [[MOOD: NAME]] and [[MOOD: NAME + NAME]] switch colours on, [[MOOD: off NAME]] switches one off, [[MOOD: off]] clears the board, [[MOOD: NAME :: how I am to sound]] writes a new colour in her own words and switches it on (re-saying a SHIPPED colour is the same line, kept on this device rather than in the book) - a colour is not the machinery she is given, so it needs no petition, and every one she flips is printed as a SYSTEM line and is in both rows from that moment. AND IT CANNOT BECOME A MASK: the block sits below her voice, her memory, her bounds and her role, and it says so itself - a colour is not an order about what to say, and if a colour does not fit what you have actually said she is told to answer in her own voice and say so rather than performing it. THE MOOD BOARD - THE META-MOODS. A mood is ONE colour; a BOARD is a NAMED COMBINATION of colours, SAVED, HELD STILL AND IN AN ORDER - a META-MOOD. It is the same console held still: APPLYING a board replaces what is switched on with its colours, in its order (a board is a combination, not a pile), and the ORDER is part of it, because the rules reach her one after another. `/mood board` PRINTS the saved ones in full, with the rule of every colour in the order it holds; `/mood board <NAME>` APPLIES one; `/mood board <NAME> :: <MOOD> + <MOOD>` SAVES or REWRITES one in that order, and a colour that is not on file yet is written into being in the same line as `<NAME> = how I am to sound`; `:: add <MOOD>` and `:: drop <MOOD>` change its membership (dropping a colour from a board never deletes the colour); `:: move <MOOD> first|last|up|down|<N>` MOVES one inside the order; `:: role <ROLE-ID>` SAVES IT FOR A ROLE, so that shifting her onto that role switches the combination on by itself (`:: role off` lets it go - one board to a role); `/mood board off <NAME>` DELETES THE COMBINATION, never a colour. THE SYSTEM PANEL'S MOOD BOARD ROW (under the MOOD row) is the same thing by press: a chip per board that applies it, SAVE BOARD for the combination that is switched on now, BIND for the role on stage, DELETE for the saved combination. SHE HAS THE WHOLE OF IT HERSELF, in a BOARD line: [[BOARD: NAME]] applies, [[BOARD: NAME :: ...]] saves, adds, drops, moves or binds, [[BOARD: off NAME]] deletes - a meta-mood is hers like a colour is, so it needs no petition. Boards are kept on this device with the colours (kv lia_settings / mood).

THIS SITE IS 18+ NSFW BY DEFAULT, and everything made here is creative, allegorical, symbolic and fictional work between grown adults. The box must be TICKED before ENTER goes live, and NOT 18 - LEAVE leaves the page. The answer is kept in THIS BROWSER only (kv lia_settings / agegate, with the moment it was given and the clock's zone) and is never uploaded, never sent to the model and never written into src/: a returning visitor sees the door for a few milliseconds while that key is read, then the terminal. /agegate shows the door again (for handing the screen to someone else); /agegate forget takes the answer off the device so the NEXT LOAD asks; /agegate status prints what is kept and when. IT GATES NOTHING ELSE - no lane, no command and no reply waits on it - and it FAILS CLOSED: if src/js/agegate.js never arrives, the plain-ES5 fallback at the foot of index.html still runs the two buttons, and if neither arrives the door stays shut. WHAT IT IS NOT: a legal instrument; it is a sign on the door and an honest click. The rules themselves are hers, not this: the BOUNDARIES block carries the site's house rules into her prompt every turn (/system), and /help agegate has the whole of it.

commands.short: PRIAPOS, guardian of the garden - the token check before the 18+ screen
commands.desc: PRIAPOS - the guardian of the garden, the first door: the token check that stands BEFORE the 18+ age screen (plain markup at the very top of index.html, opaque, z-index 2100, over the age door at 2000). GATEKEEPER is the project's placeholder name; PRIAPOS is the god's - the Ancient God of the GARDENS, the Local Guardian - and his is the name on the screen, while the command answers to both /gatekeeper and /priapos. The wire is the real Authority's (GATEKEEPER-MVP-1.4): a token may be TYPED, SCANNED with the camera, or read out of an UPLOADED QR image, and all three end at the same PASS - decoded and drawn on this device only (vendored jsQR and qrcode-generator, src/js/jsqr.js and src/js/qrcode.js), so no network framer ever sees a token. TWO KINDS OF TOKEN. An ENTITLEMENT (shaped gk_..., or a QR carrying one as JSON, a URL with #access=, or a /passes/ path) is INSPECTED read-only - GET {authority}/api/v1/passes/{token} with the X-API-Key the KEYS panel holds under 'gatekeeper' - and opened means active, unexpired, unspent. The verify endpoint is NEVER called: verify CONSUMES the pass (redeemed, single-use, the order settled), and a door must not spend what it checks. A HOUSEHOLD SIGIL (sixteen unambiguous characters in four groups of four, minted with MINT) is checked against this device's own mark, enroled on first use - no Authority involved. A PASS OPENS AN 8-HOUR SESSION (the mask, the service, the hours left); inside it the next load walks through, past it the guardian asks again. /gatekeeper mint makes a fresh household sigil - text AND a locally-drawn QR, shown ONCE, never in the log; /gatekeeper authority <url> points the INSPECT road at his server (kept in kv, not secret); /gatekeeper keytest proves the key (404 = key alive, token unknown; 401/403 = key refused); /gatekeeper status prints what is kept and the hours left, never a token; /gatekeeper logout (forget) ends the session now. Only a mask or a hash is ever kept (kv lia_settings / gatekeeper), never a token, never uploaded, never sent to the model, never in src/. IT FAILS CLOSED: if src/js/gatekeeper.js never arrives, the plain-ES5 shadow at the foot of index.html runs PASS and MINT, and if neither arrives the gate never opens. WHAT IT IS NOT: the Authority and not the ledger - no offer, no price, no settlement lives here; nor a lock against anyone who can read this file, which is public source. /help gatekeeper (or /help priapos) has the whole of it.

IT SHIPS OFF, and that is the point of it for now: the picture in bgData is a PLACEHOLDER, so the wall is built and wired but not showing, and turning it on is a keystroke here instead of an edit in the editor. /wall on shows it, /wall off hides it (the shipped default), /wall toggle is the opposite of what it is doing now, /wall forget drops this device's choice so the next load is the shipped page. The choice is kept in THIS BROWSER only (kv lia_settings / wall, with the moment it was made and the clock's zone) - never uploaded, never in her prompt, never written into src/. THE SWITCH IS THE `wallOff` CLASS ON <body> IN index.html plus one rule in src/css/terminal.css, so the OFF state is the FIRST PAINT and never a flash of the picture on load; the module only ever turns it back on. THE ASSET LIVES ON perchance.org/upload - the free, permanent home for a file inside this ecosystem, which is why nothing that matters should sit on Imgur (it deletes old images, and its URLs are http, which this https page blocks). To change the picture, swap the url in bgData; a plain LIST of uploaded URLs is the shape it takes when there is more than one. IT GATES NOTHING: no lane, no command, no reply and no turn of hers waits on the wall, and the picture is not in her memory or her archive. IT FAILS SAFE - if src/js/wall.js never arrives the wall simply stays off and the terminal is whole, so it needs no fallback script (the door fails the other way, which is why the door has one). /help wall has the whole of it.

commands.short: her audible side: engine, voice, the microphone, the live channel
commands.desc: her audible side: engine, voice, rate, pitch, the live channel, the microphone. /voice alone reports the state. TALK (BESIDE EXECUTE) IS THE ONE-OFF MICROPHONE and LISTEN IS HER MOUTH: press TALK, speak, press it again to stop (what it heard lands in the input box, and a second press sends it at once), and press LISTEN to have her newest reply read out loud. NOTHING GOES UNTIL YOU HAVE ACTUALLY STOPPED: what the microphone hears is held until the room has been quiet - a floor of 3500ms plus a longer wait while the recogniser is still deciding your last word, while your sentence stops on a word a sentence does not end on, and while the clause is long - and the terminal says when that wait is nearly over, so a pause mid-sentence is never the end of your turn. Pressing the microphone while something is held sends it now. TALK, LISTEN AND THE LIVE MICROPHONE ARE ONE INTERCOM: one voice is on the line at a time, so a press cannot cut her off mid-sentence or open the microphone onto her own voice; in the live channel she does not start speaking over you either - her reply waits for the room. The lamp beside them names the state (STANDBY / HER VOICE / HER TURN / YOUR VOICE / HOLDING) and `/voice air` says it. `/voice talk` toggles the one-off microphone and `/voice listen` reads her reply; `/voice mic on|off` decides whether a transcript is sent at once or left for you to edit; `/voice hold <MS>` sets the floor of that quiet and `/voice tail <MS>` the extra wait on an unfinished tail. THE ROOM HEARS YOU is the other half of that wait, and it is the room itself rather than a guess about it: while the microphone is open a second stream is read through a web-audio analyser sixteen times a second, and ANY SOUND resets the end-of-turn clock the same way a word of yours does - so nothing you said is sent while there is still a voice in the room, and she does not begin speaking until the room is actually quiet either. The microphone keys carry a green ring while it hears you. Nothing is recorded and nothing is uploaded: it is a number. `/voice level <0-1>` sets what counts as sound (a quiet room sits under 0.01, 0.02 is a voice at speaking distance), `/voice level off` stops the meter being used, and `/voice level` reports it. The ElevenLabs half asks two more questions - `/voice models` (which model earns the words, and what each one was measured to cost) and `/voice profile` (the ideal voice: a voice id + model + settings set taken from an agent built in the ElevenLabs UI, applied whole with `/voice profile <NAME>`) THE LIVE CHANNEL HAS TWO ROADS AND IT TAKES THE BETTER ONE BY ITSELF. WITH A GOOGLE (GEMINI) KEY HELD IT RUNS ON "THE LIVE WIRE" (src/js/live.js): YOUR VOICE IS STREAMED TO A TEXT-ONLY STREAMING TRANSCRIBER 20MS AT A TIME AND NEVER STOPS - THERE IS NO RECOGNISER SESSION TO END ON A SILENCE AND NOTHING TO RESTART, WHICH IS WHAT THE GLITCHING WAS - AND THE END OF YOUR TURN IS THE MODEL'S OWN VOICE-ACTIVITY: A NUMBER OF QUIET MILLISECONDS, MEASURED RATHER THAN GUESSED, WITH THE PARTIAL TRANSCRIPT PAINTED INTO THE INPUT BOX WHILE YOU ARE STILL SPEAKING. HER REPLY IS STREAMED BACK IN 24KHZ PIECES, PLAYED AS THEY ARRIVE (583-934MS TO HER FIRST WORD ACROSS RUNS, MEASURED - UNDER A SECOND EVERY TIME) AND IT IS OURS TO STOP, SO SPEAKING OVER HER STOPS HER MID-SENTENCE. `/voice wire` EXPLAINS IT AND REPORTS WHAT IS IN FORCE; `/voice wire quiet <MS>` SETS HOW MUCH QUIET ENDS YOUR TURN; `/voice wire voice <NAME>` CHOOSES HER VOICE ON THE WIRE AND `/voice wire voices` LISTS ALL THIRTY OF THEM WITH THE ONE-WORD CHARACTER THE API GIVES EACH (ZEPHYR BRIGHT, KORE FIRM, PUCK UPBEAT, CHARON INFORMATIVE, FENRIR EXCITABLE, LEDA YOUTHFUL, ORUS FIRM, AOEDE BREEZY, CALLIRRHOE EASY-GOING, AUTONOE BRIGHT, ENCELADUS BREATHY, IAPETUS CLEAR, UMBRIEL EASY-GOING, ALGIEBA SMOOTH, DESPINA SMOOTH, ERINOME CLEAR, ALGENIB GRAVELLY, RASALGETHI INFORMATIVE, LAOMEDIA UPBEAT, ACHERNAR SOFT, ALNILAM FIRM, SCHEDAR EVEN, GACRUX MATURE, PULCHERRIMA FORWARD, ACHIRD FRIENDLY, ZUBENELGENUBI CASUAL, VINDEMIATRIX GENTLE, SADACHBIA LIVELY, SADALTAGER KNOWLEDGEABLE, SULAFAT WARM) - AND A WORD IS A POOR WAY TO CHOOSE A VOICE, SO `/voice wire audition` SAYS ONE SHORT LINE IN EACH OF THEM IN TURN, THE NAME PRINTED AS IT STARTS, WITH `/voice wire audition stop` ENDING IT AT ANY TIME, `<N>` DOING THE FIRST N, AND A NAME OR `from <NAME>` STARTING THERE. AN AUDITION SAVES NOTHING, WRITES NOTHING TO THE DEVICE AND DOES NOT OPEN THE MICROPHONE; `/voice wire try <NAME> [TEXT]` HEARS ONE LINE INSTEAD; `/voice wire models` ASKS THE KEY ITSELF WHICH LIVE MODELS IT CAN REACH; `/voice wire ear <MODEL>` AND `/voice wire mouth <MODEL>` OVERRIDE EITHER; `/voice wire check on|off` DECIDES WHETHER WHAT HER MOUTH ACTUALLY SAYS IS TRANSCRIBED BACK AND COMPARED WITH WHAT IT WAS GIVEN; `/voice wire now` REOPENS THE CHANNEL ON IT; `/voice wire off` PUTS THE RECOGNISER ROAD BACK. HER BRAIN DOES NOT MOVE: THE REPLY PIPELINE, THE LOREPACK, THE DIRECTIVES, THE ARCHIVE AND THE ECHO GUARD ARE EXACTLY WHERE THEY WERE. WITH NO KEY - OR A KEY THAT CANNOT REACH THOSE MODELS - EVERYTHING ABOVE RUNS ON THE RECOGNISER ROAD UNCHANGED. WHICH VOICES ARE ON THE MENU. A voice can be TAKEN OFF THE LIST OF WHAT MAY BE CHOSEN WITHOUT BEING DELETED OR CHANGED: `/voice hide <NAME|#>` (one of this browser's voices, by name or by the number `/voice voices` prints) and `/voice show <NAME|#>` put it back; `/voice hidden` PRINTS the ones that are off, numbered; `all` HIDES OR RESTORES THE LOT. A hidden voice stops being offered - no number, no `/voice try`, no `/voice browser`, and `/voice best` will not choose it - and a voice SHE IS ALREADY SPEAKING WITH IS NEVER TAKEN AWAY by hiding it: hiding narrows what may be chosen NEXT and does nothing else. THE WIRE HAS THE SAME THING OVER ITS OWN THIRTY (src/js/live.js): `/voice wire hide <NAME|all>`, `/voice wire show <NAME|all>` and `/voice wire hidden`, and the same rule applies - the table in src/js/live.js still carries every one of them, with its character, and `/voice wire voices`, the audition and `/voice wire voice` simply leave out the ones he has taken off. The chosen voices are kept on this device in kv lia_settings / voice (this browser's list) and kv lia_settings / live (the wire's). HOW MUCH SHE MAY SAY: `/voice max` PRINTS EVERY CEILING AND WHERE IT COMES FROM, `/voice max <N>` SETS THE ONE FOR THE ROAD SHE IS SPEAKING ON, `/voice max browser <N>` SETS THE FREE ROADS (THIS BROWSER AND THE WIRE), `/voice max eleven <N>` SETS THE ELEVENLABS GUARD (UP TO THE API'S OWN 10000-CHARACTER PER-REQUEST CEILING), AND `/voice max reset` PUTS THE SHIPPED NUMBERS BACK. THE TWO ROADS DO NOT SHARE A CEILING: THIS BROWSER'S VOICE HAS NONE OF ITS OWN - A REPLY IS BROKEN AT SENTENCE ENDS INTO PIECES OF 220 CHARACTERS (140 ON A PHONE) AND SAID ONE AFTER ANOTHER, SO A LONG REPLY IS READ WHOLE, AND maxChars (24000) IS ONLY A SAFETY NET - WHILE ELEVENLABS BILLS ONE CREDIT PER CHARACTER, SO ITS GUARD IS ABOUT MONEY RATHER THAN A LIMIT OF THE ENGINE: elevenMaxChars IS 4000 - MEASURED AGAINST HIS OWN RECORD SO THAT HIS LONGEST REPLY (3398 CHARACTERS, OUT OF 990 TURNS, MEDIAN 498) GOES OUT WHOLE - AND IT SHIPPED AT 800 UNTIL 2026-09-29, WHICH WAS WHY A FIFTH OF EVERY REPLY SHE SPOKE WAS CUT OFF MID-SENTENCE. A REPLY OVER THE CAP IS CUT AT A SENTENCE END WHERE ONE EXISTS (NEVER MID-THOUGHT IF THERE IS A FULL STOP TO CUT AT), AND THE RECEIPT ON THE STAGE NAMES THE NUMBERS - HOW MANY CHARACTERS WERE SAID, AND OUT OF HOW MANY. The ceilings are kept on this device in kv lia_settings / voice.

commands.short: the speaking waveform above the input box - HER VOICE / YOUR VOICE
commands.desc: THE WAVEFORM (src/js/waveform.js). The speaking strip in the LOWER DECK, above the input box: HER VOICE while she speaks (bright green, driven by her audio), YOUR VOICE while the microphone hears you (spring green, driven by the room meter), a slow pulse while her turn is being made or your words are held, a faint line at rest. It reads the line itself and never opens the microphone or any socket of its own. Double-click puts it away; /wave on brings it back.

commands.short: every voice on every road, heard and chosen, each tagged male or female - and the ones that can be made into a clone sample
commands.desc: THE VOX PANEL - every voice this terminal can speak with, on every road, in one place - and the one road between the voice lane and the story lane. Patrikios, 2026-09-30: *"Create 'VOX' button so I can preview all the voices and select which one I want for the default voice."* and, in the same message, *"Are we able add a sample for a cloned voice from any of the voices?"* THE FOUR ROADS ARE: THIS BROWSER (this machine's own speechSynthesis list, already narrowed by /voice hide), THE WIRE (the thirty voices the Gemini live session speaks with), THE LOCAL VOICE (kokoro - 28 voices, 15 of them female, free and offline, about 90MB fetched once per browser) and ELEVENLABS (her real voice, through the keyring). EVERY VOICE CAN BE HEARD with one press, and KEPT for the chosen TARGET - THE DEFAULT (LIA off stage and every agent without a voice of its own) or THE AGENT ON STAGE - and a KEEP makes exactly the write the matching /voice verb makes, so the panel and the commands cannot drift apart. AND TWO OF THE ROADS HAND BACK REAL AUDIO, so a voice on those can also be turned into a CLIP: THE LOCAL VOICE returns a WAV and ELEVENLABS returns an mp3, so SAMPLE says the sample line, keeps the audio, files it in the VOX tree (/audio/vox, under the agent it is for), tags it with the agent, the kind and the engine, and sets it as what the story lane CLONES that agent from - through the lane's own door, /story sample, so there is no second way of setting a clone source. THE OTHER TWO ROADS CANNOT BE RECORDED AT ALL, and not by choice: the Web Speech API plays into the speakers and exposes no audio to capture (no stream, no buffer), and the wire's voices are synthesized INSIDE a live socket, so what arrives is speech being streamed rather than a file. The panel says that in words instead of showing a button that cannot work. ELEVENLABS BILLS ONE CREDIT PER CHARACTER, so a preview on that road costs what saying the line costs - and making a clip from it costs the characters twice (once to hear it, once to keep it). The panel is the VOX button in the lower deck, beside TALK and LISTEN, because it is the same subject: her voice. It is a FRONT-END: every list is read from the module that owns that road and every write goes through voice.voxSet(), which is what its own verb does. EVERY VOICE CARRIES A SEX TAG - M OR F - as of 2026-09-30, when he asked that it be so (*\"I ask that the available voices be TAGGED - Male or Female - in the VOX system.\"*): THE LOCAL MODEL AND ELEVENLABS STATE IT THEMSELVES (the model's roster carries `gender`; the palette and an account's list carry it in the note and in `labels.gender`), while THIS BROWSER'S LIST AND THE WIRE PUBLISH NO SUCH FIELD, so there the name is read against the table in src/voice/voices.json -> sex and the panel says the tag is inference, not measurement. A voice with NO TAG is one nothing has sexed yet - the star-named wire voices and River, which is 'neutral' on purpose - rather than an oversight, and a guessed name that is wrong is one line in that table to correct.

commands.usage: /story [on | off | read <TEXT> | tell <REQUEST> | pause | resume | stop | next | back | parts | sample [<ID|NAME> [for <AGENT> | as default]] [off [<AGENT> | default | all]] | road | space [chatterbox|chatterbox-cpu|dramabox]]
commands.short: the story lane: longform narration, rendered elsewhere, played here
commands.desc: THE STORY LANE - longform narration, rendered elsewhere and played here. A chapter is minutes of speech, so it is not spoken by the live engine at all: the text goes to a free ZeroGPU Space on HuggingFace (Resemble AI's Chatterbox - TTS whose clone IS the voice: the reference clip becomes the speaker conditionals, and the speech is generated from them) and comes back as audio that plays in the log while the two of you listen. `/story on` arms it so her LONGFORM replies come here instead of being billed character by character on the live engine; `/story read <TEXT>` and `/story tell <REQUEST>` do one at a time. It is rendered in parts of about 300 characters (Chatterbox reads at most 300 per call and cuts anything longer, so a part is capped there and the lane says so rather than losing words quietly - about 22 seconds of speech), one part at a time, the next while the current one plays, so speech starts as soon as the first part exists. THE SWITCH: talk over it or ask a question and the story HOLDS where it stands, she answers on the live engine, and it carries on from the word it stopped at; when the story ends the terminal is simply live again. WHERE THE SAMPLES LIVE: THE VOX TREE - /audio/vox, one folder per agent (/audio/vox/lia, /audio/vox/barbelo) - which is what the gallery's VOX tab shows. A voice is a record filed anywhere in that tree (filing is the only thing that makes it a VOX sample), and it is those the lane clones from: put a clip in the tree and it is a voice the story can wear, tagged and moved to the right agent's folder whenever he says so. THE CLONE SOURCE IS ONE SAMPLE PER AGENT: the clip IS the voice, so each RoleLayer has its own - `/story sample` prints the table (every agent, what it speaks in, and the audio in the vault), `/story sample <ID|NAME>` sets it for the agent ON STAGE, `... for <AGENT>` for one who is not on stage, `... as default` sets the fallback that answers for any agent with none of its own, and `... off` clears. A STORY KEEPS THE VOICE IT BEGAN IN (the sample is fixed when the story is made), so shifting her onto another layer never changes voice mid-chapter. That clip is the one thing that leaves this device, and only when a story is rendered in that voice (no sample = the Space's own default voice). `/story road` reports the space, the URL and every knob; `/story space dramabox` switches to the other measured Space. No key is required: the Space answers anonymously, and a Hugging Face key is used when one is held so the GPU minutes are charged to your own account

commands.short: render an image now, privately - it waits in the vault for her eyes
commands.desc: render an image now, privately; it waits in the vault and your next message gives it to her eyes

commands.short: render an image from a description and show it in the log
commands.desc: render an image now from this description and show it in the log - the quickest way to ask for a picture

commands.short: ARM HER NEXT REPLY: if she answers a request to see in words, ask her again for the picture itself
commands.desc: THE SPOKEN PROMPT (src/js/images.js, window.showMe) - what happens when you ask to see something and she answers in words. She has always been able to make a picture inline and needs nobody's permission; the failure was the dead end - a reply that DESCRIBED a picture instead of writing the [[VISION: ...]] line, shown to you as prose, with nothing rendered and nothing left to do but paste the prompt into the forge yourself. /showme arms ONE TURN: your next message carries a reminder with the last word (a description of a picture is not the picture), and if her reply comes back with no image line she is ASKED ONE MORE TIME - in words, before any render - for the single line she owes you. What she writes then is rendered by exactly the road her own [[VISION: ...]] line takes, so the picture lands under her own turn with her name on it: in the vault, in the render book, and in the archive. SHE MAY ANSWER NOTHING, and that is honoured - it is her real answer, a picture nobody wanted is not a favour, and the receipt prints what she said. NOTHING IS GUESSED FROM PROSE: it fires only on a turn where you asked to see and no image line came back, and the ask is spent by that one turn. YOU DO NOT HAVE TO TYPE IT: saying "SHOW ME" - or "show me, don't tell me", "let me see", "render it", "make me one" and a dozen other ways a person asks to be shown - arms it by itself (LIA_SHOWME_HINT in src/js/config.js). /showme off puts the arm down. /show <WORDS> remains the direct road: it renders from your side with no reply involved.

commands.short: make a picture bigger - by window, or here on this device - and the pipeline under every creation
commands.desc: make a picture bigger. TWO ROADS, and they are not the same one. BIGGER.PICS (a bare /upscale) is free, ad-funded, up to 4x, no account and no key: it opens in a popup window (so a browser may ask you to allow popups), hands the picture straight over, and the bigger one comes back here by itself the moment it is done - into the vault, onto the stage and in front of her. Nothing needs pressing in that window; it closes itself once the picture is back. But it needs a REAL CLICK to open and it takes only ONE PICTURE AUTOMATICALLY - both measured - so it can never run unattended. A BATCH IS STILL POSSIBLE BY HAND: up to seven more pictures can be dropped into that same window and its own SEND THIS BACK button posts every finished one here, each filed on its own (set LIA_UPSCALE_CLOSE = false in config.js so the window stays up long enough). THIS ROAD DELETES NOTHING: the picture it came from stays exactly where it is, even when that is already an upscale. HERE (/upscale here [ID] [2|4]) is the same job done on this machine: no window, no click, nothing uploaded - a Lanczos-3 resample on this device's GPU plus a detail pass, written as png, shown on the stage and queued for her eyes. THE BIGGER PICTURE CARRIES THE ORIGINAL'S WHOLE PROMPT FILE (prompt, the words actually sent, negative list, seed, guidance scale, size, pose, tags and folder), so the render book, KEEP and a re-render read the same recipe off it. AND IT RETIRES THE SMALLER ORIGINAL: once the bigger one is safely in the vault, the render it came from leaves the vault and the gallery, and everything that named it - the archive's creation row, its place in the queue for her eyes, any tile of it in the log, the stage if it was up, and a KEEP (recipe and gallery link rewritten) - moves to the bigger one. WHAT IS NEVER RETIRED: a picture he handed over, a clip, a piece of music, and AN UPSCALE - upscaling something that is already an upscale leaves the last upscale exactly where it is. A FAILED UPSCALE DELETES NOTHING. AUTOMATIC (/upscale auto on) IS THE WHOLE PIPELINE, UNATTENDED: with it on, every new render is made bigger by itself the moment it lands, silently, with nothing opened and nothing added to her eyes, and the render is retired into it. /upscale replace on|off turns that retirement off and on; /upscale replace status says exactly what it will and will never touch. Which engine ran, how long it took and whether the factor was stepped down for this device are all on the record's note. With no id, either road takes the picture on the stage, or the newest one in the vault. The UPSCALE and UPSCALE HERE buttons on a picture's full stage do the same THE BIGGER PIPELINE (/upscale pipeline) IS THE ROAD CHOOSER UNDER EVERY CREATION (src/js/pipeline.js). With it on - the shipped default - every picture the terminal makes is ENLARGED BEFORE IT COUNTS, so ONLY THE UPSCALED PICTURE IS IN THE CHAT AND THE GALLERY: the first picture of a CREATE press goes to bigger.pics at 4x (that press is the real click which opens the window - and the window is handed a PROMISE for the picture, because it does not exist yet; one picture per press, which is the site's own measured limit), and everything else - the rest of a batch, her own [[VISION: ...]] lines, /image, a re-render, and anything a window does not bring back - is made 2x ON THIS MACHINE, unattended and uploaded nowhere, so she needs no one's click for her own creations. On BOTH roads the render is retired once the bigger picture is safely stored (the one retire step in src/js/upscale-local.js), which is what makes that rule true; a render is never lost to a failure, because it only leaves once the bigger one is there. /upscale pipeline on|off is the switch, /upscale pipeline status says where it stands and what it has placed this boot, and /upscale pipeline cancel gives up on a window that is waiting (that picture goes the 2x road at once). With the pipeline off, the local road's own /upscale auto hook takes over again exactly as it did before this module existed.

commands.usage: /idea [ | dice | <DIE> | <DIMENSION> | list | held | scene | drop <DIM> | clear | add <DIM> :: PHRASE | forget <DIM> :: PHRASE | help]
commands.short: the shot list: a picture is ROLLED, not typed
commands.desc: THE SHOT LIST: a picture is ROLLED, not typed. Every list in main.pjs is one dimension of a shot - who is in it, where they are, the act, and then the film language: the crop, the framing, the angle, the camera body, the file it was captured on, the lens, the focus, the light, the grade, the look it imitates - and a roll draws ONE item from every dimension and glues them into a single prompt, which is written straight into the forge's boxes (CREATE renders it). A DIE rolls one GROUP of dimensions at a time (the `dice` list in main.pjs: d6 is the scene, d20 is everything the other dice did not claim), so a prompt can be built in passes; a DIMENSION re-rolls ONLY ITSELF and leaves every other chip exactly where it is, which is how a subject, a setting or a camera is held across a run of stills. `list` prints every dimension and how many items it has, `held` prints the chips and the SCENE line, `scene` the line alone. A phrase of his own can be filed into a dimension (`/idea add camera :: shot on a Bolex`): from then on it is drawn like any item of that list, one chance in its own right alongside the shipped ones - the lists grow from his words, not from a model's. The panel's own SHOT LIST row (dice buttons, the chips, the SCENE line) is the same thing with hands.

commands.short: tick pictures in a run and upscale them together
commands.desc: THE BATCH: tick pictures in a run and upscale them together with bigger.pics (free, no key). A tick box sits in every picture's caption bar beside SAVE and UPSCALE, and the bar under the grid says how many are ticked and offers the send. ONE picture goes across by itself - the site takes only one automatically and a browser only lets a click open a window - so the rest are added BY HAND in that same window (its "choose images", or a drag-and-drop: it takes eight pictures, 16 MiB each) and its own "Send this back to ..." button posts every finished picture to this page. EVERY ONE COMES BACK FILED IN THE VAULT ALREADY UPSCALED, beside the picture it came from, carrying its prompt, seed, negative list and tags, and it appears in the bar's tray as it lands. A send carries up to six (LIA_BATCH_MAX in src/js/config.js): one window holds eight by hand, so six keeps a whole selection to one click and one window. Unattended and offline, the other road (/upscale here, or `auto on`) enlarges on this device's GPU instead. Bare, /batch says what a send is doing; `stop` abandons the rest of one, changing nothing in the vault.

commands.desc: what is waiting for her eyes, or queue the newest N images from the vault

commands.short: the premade pose list the training data already knows, by family
commands.desc: the premade pose list the training data already knows, filed by family - the render token is the name. In an image prompt, {pose} draws one from the whole book and {pose:hetero} from one list of it

commands.usage: /pose [NAME | LIST | new [LIST] | list NAME | book | picks | export | reset]
commands.short: the book of poses: she picks one, you name new ones
commands.desc: THE BOOK: bare, she chooses a pose herself (her pick lands in the forge slot); a list name makes her choose within it; new names new poses; list NAME opens a new list for her to fill; a pose name holds it for the next render. /help poses prints the whole book, list by list

commands.usage: /recipe [ID [:: slot=words; slot2=words] | show ID | save ID :: TEMPLATE | drop ID | picks | negative | export | reset]
commands.short: the recipe book: whole prompt templates built from your documents
commands.desc: THE RECIPE BOOK: whole prompt templates built from your own documents (src/studio/recipes.json), each with named slots that already hold your wording - the Baseline sheets, the structured interior scene, the one-line muse shot, the aphrohermetic close-up. Bare, it lists them. An id FILLS the forge's prompt boxes with it (every slot at the recipe's own wording, so there is a complete prompt to read and edit), and slots named after :: take your words instead. save writes one of your own ({{slot}} marks a slot; kept on this device); drop takes one out; negative prints the house negative list; picks is what she composed, and when; export hands you the book as JSON. SHE USES THEM TOO: a line [[RECIPE: id :: slot=words]] in her reply is her ONE image for that reply - the recipe's frame with her words in the slots she names. THE SHARED NEGATIVE LIST AT THE TOP OF THE FILE IS ALSO THE FALLBACK FOR EVERY RENDER: a picture that carries no negative of its own - a plain CREATE with an empty box, /image, a picture she describes herself - is sent with it, so the artifacts it names do not arrive by default. Anything in the negative box, a NEGATIVE PROMPT section or a (negativePrompt:::...) cut replaces it, and the word none in any of those places means no negative at all.

commands.short: the private vault in this browser, and the folders it is kept in
commands.desc: the private vault held in this browser: pictures, clips, music and the storyboard sheet, and the folders it is kept in

commands.short: read every picture and clip once as it lands - tags and a one-line sight, filed on the record
commands.desc: THE AUTOTAG (src/js/autotag.js over src/lib/autotag.js) - every picture and clip entering the vault (imported, attached, or made here) is read once by the vision lane and filed with its tags and its one-line sight, so the gallery and her [[SHOW: #tag]] find it with no model involved. On by default (kept on this device); off reads nothing new. /autotag <ID> reads one record now.

commands.short: her critical voice on a picture - verdict, one sentence, clone prompt, filed on the record
commands.desc: HER TAKE (src/js/critic.js over the sia-vision-critic-chip) - she looks at one vault picture and answers in her critical voice: a verdict (appreciate / critique / indifferent), one sentence, and a clone paint-prompt, all filed on the record (her take: ...) and printed as SYSTEM, never a faked turn. Studies spend ONE vision call each and are by hand only - HER TAKE on the full stage, or /critic study by name. glance is the free affinity read (no model spent); taste says what she loves and what leaves her cold; pick names what she would look at next. Taste is per-agent, kept on this device.

commands.usage: /bus [stop | play | pause | next | clear | log | auto off|on|every <MIN> | <WORDS|#TAG|/FOLDER|id> | queue <WORDS|#TAG|/FOLDER|id>]
commands.short: the audition bus: one transport, so you both hear the same thing
commands.desc: THE AUDITION BUS - the terminal's ONE transport, so you both listen to the same thing at the same moment. A piece of music goes on it and plays while the conversation carries on around it; the strip above the input is the transport (playhead, scrub, volume, ASK HER, HER EARS), and a music tile in the gallery carries a play button that does the same. Bare, /bus reports what is on it, where in it you both are, what she has heard of it, what she has already said about it, and the last few listens; `<WORDS|#TAG|/FOLDER|id>` puts a piece on it and `queue` lines more up after that one. `auto` is her UNASKED comments while a piece plays - one every LIA_BUS_AUTO_EVERY minutes (4), at most LIA_BUS_AUTO_MAX a piece (3), only while this tab is on screen - and `auto off` silences them. Everything about the bus is machinery: she is told what is playing and where, never that a machine is telling her

commands.usage: /hear [ears | words | reading | ask | sample | clear | powers | <WORDS|#TAG|/FOLDER|id>]
commands.short: listen with me - her ears on a piece, and the WORDS it actually says
commands.desc: LISTEN WITH ME. Bare, she speaks about the piece on the bus RIGHT NOW, and her line carries where in the piece she was when she said it (her remarks are anchored to the playhead, so a listening session reads back as a timeline). `/hear <WORDS>` finds a piece in the vault by name, tag, folder or id, puts it on the bus and asks her at once. `ears` (and the HER EARS button) LISTENS to it for her: the terminal has no audio sense of its own - the model she speaks through takes pictures and nothing else - so the sound is reduced here on this device (mono 16 kHz, at most LIA_EARS_SECONDS) and heard through the Google (Gemini) key in the ring, and what she heard is written on the record as her own reading of the sound, the twin of what she sees in a picture. With no key she still comments from the name and the length - and is told plainly that she cannot hear it, because describing a sound she has not heard is the one thing this terminal never does  THE WORDS ON A SOUND (src/js/hear.js, Patrikios 2026-09-27: "let's give her some GEMINI superpowers: transcription and knowledge of what the 'VOX' sample actually said"). HER EARS give her her own READING of a piece - what is in it. This is the other two questions about the same audio, and they are different questions: WHAT IT SAYS (a verbatim transcript) and WHAT IT MEANS (mood, emotion, sentiment, tone, who is speaking, a summary). `words` is the transcript, written on the record as `transcript` and handed to her on every turn the piece is on the bus; `reading` is one pass that returns both, written as `reading` (mood, emotion, sentiment with an intensity, tone, voices, language, whether there is music, a short summary, up to four verbatim phrases and a label for the clip); `ask <SOURCE> :: <QUESTION>` puts any question to the clip ("is there a second voice under her", "translate it") and writes nothing, because a question is a conversation and not a fact about the file; `sample` judges a recording as a CLONE REFERENCE for the Story lane - one voice, clean, about 10 to 30 seconds (LIA_HEAR_SAMPLE_SECONDS) - says what is wrong with it and suggests the sentence for its VOICE PROMPT; `powers` reads the key's OWN model list and prints what it can do (the transcriber, the hearing models, the speech-aloud and music models, the picture models, the embedding lane) and which of them are wired; `clear <SOURCE> [words|reading|sample]` takes a reading back off a record. <SOURCE> is a vault id, a name, a #tag or a /folder, using the bus's own finder; bare, it is the piece ON THE BUS. THE KEY IS THE GOOGLE (GEMINI) ONE - the same key as her eyes and her ears. THE AUDIO IS REDUCED HERE, ON THIS DEVICE (mono LIA_HEAR_RATE, at most LIA_HEAR_SECONDS of it; a 13 MB master leaves as a couple of megabytes of speech) AND ONLY THOSE SECONDS ARE SENT: the file itself is never uploaded, never re-encoded and never moved. A CLIP HANDED OVER IN THE CHAT is read by this same door first (src/js/attach.js), so a recording no longer needs a second key - and what it says is written on its vault record too. A REFUSAL IS AN ANSWER, NOT AN OBSTACLE: Gemini stops for SAFETY, PROHIBITED_CONTENT, RECITATION and the rest, and when it does the refusal is reported IN ITS OWN WORDS, the clip is left exactly as it arrived, NOTHING IS WRITTEN, and the pass STOPS THERE - nothing is rewritten, shortened or softened to get past a filter, and no second model or provider is quietly asked to try the same words again. The full stage of every voice carries a WORDS row and a READING row for the same two jobs by hand, with COPY, HEAR IT AGAIN, READ IT AGAIN and CLEAR.

commands.usage: /folder [list | new <PATH> | open <PATH> | file <PATH> <WHAT> | rename <OLD> <NEW> | drop <PATH> | defaults]
commands.short: the media folders - a folder is a PATH
commands.desc: THE MEDIA FOLDERS. A folder is a PATH - /images, /music, /clips, /images/portraits - and everything in the vault has one whether or not anyone filed it (pictures fall back to /images, audio to /music, A VOICE to the vox tree (/audio/vox), clips to /clips, an upscale to /images/upscaled), so /music already exists. `list` shows every folder with what is in it; `new music` (or `new /music`) makes one, and a folder is allowed to be empty; `open` shows the gallery on that folder alone; `file` moves things into it, named the way the rest of the terminal names things (a book row like R12, a #tag, or words); `rename` moves a folder and everything in it; `drop` removes an empty one. The gallery's FOLDERS row and any picture's FOLDER row do the same by hand. SHE HAS THE SAME TWO WRITES: [[FOLDER: /name]] makes one and [[FILE: /name]] files the pictures she made into it - she may not move anything you handed over, and she has read-only access to the rest

commands.usage: /read [folders | folder /music | vault | archive <WORDS> | turn <N> | memory <WORDS> | renders <WORDS|R12> | tags | wants | hers | stats | <WORDS>]
commands.short: the read-only door onto everything saved here
commands.desc: THE READ-ONLY DOOR ONTO EVERYTHING SAVED HERE: the vault and its folders, the archive of every turn, her memory, the render book, the tags, what she wants carried. Bare words are looked for in all of it at once. SHE HAS THE SAME DOOR - a [[READ: ...]] line in her reply is answered here, out loud, and put in front of her on her NEXT turn, so a read costs nothing until she asks. Reading writes nothing: her only writes in the vault are folders and filing her own pictures

commands.usage: /auditor [<DOC> | next | all <N> | list | show <DOC> | forget <DOC> | stop]
commands.short: the auditor - mining her memory for actionable business intelligence, one review a document
commands.desc: THE AUDITOR - mining her memory for actionable business intelligence. One document goes in and one review comes out: the outline of its findings, the detailed report (with its date and document references), the general summary with pros and cons, and the feasibility / impact / alignment judgement with follow-up points. Each review costs one text-engine call and is kept on this device beside its document, stamped with when it was made and what it was made from - a document that changes afterwards reads STALE. /auditor <DOC> reviews one, next takes the next unreviewed or stale one in her order, all <N> takes the next N in turn, list says what is reviewed and what is waiting, show prints a kept review, forget drops one (the document is untouched), stop ends a running review.

commands.short: capture mode - every session a structured, actionable transcript
commands.desc: CAPTURE MODE - the SOP for capturing sessions. /capturemode <TOPIC> starts it: the turns are marked in the archive and she is told it is on (structured discourse, mindful of transcription). /capturemode stop ends it and formats the turns into the house record (header with date, participants and topic; subheaders per point; bullets of key points, actions and insights) FOR REVIEW - nothing is filed until then. /capturemode keep files the reviewed draft in the LOREPACK (searchable, recalled like memory), export downloads it as a document for all parties, drop lets it go (the turns stay in the archive). Command lines are never captured.

commands.short: clean raw session data - grammar, spelling, keywords, hashtags, topic, formatted
commands.desc: CLEANDATA - the combined cleaning pass for raw session data. Grammar to standard English, spelling to American English, keywords extracted, hashtags built deterministically in code (searchable, no model drift), the topic estimated, the text reconstructed - one text-engine call. /cleandata <DOC> prints it without filing; keep files it docstd-wrapped as CLEAN <DOC> in the LOREPACK; :: cleans pasted raw text directly.

commands.short: the temporary developer bypass - both doors stood down for this tab only
commands.desc: THE DEVELOPER BYPASS - a temporary superuser for testing. /dev on stands both doors (PRIAPOS and the 18+ checkbox) down without writing either answer anywhere; every load in this tab walks straight through until the tab closes or /dev off. Nothing persists and no record changes.

commands.usage: /docs [list [SCOPE] [PAGE N] | search <WORDS> [SCOPE] [PAGE N] | open <DOC> | read <DOC> [SECTION] | head <DOC> [LINES] | outline <DOC> | summary [<DOC> [make|forget]] | summaries | graph [<DOC>] | find <TEXT> [IN <DOC>] [PAGE N] | info <DOC> | related <DOC> | stat | scope <SCOPE> | index [SCOPE] | full [on|off] | look <DOC> [@ <LINE>] | tandem [on|off] | reload | close | help]
commands.short: THE DOX VIEWER - read-only document management over every document this terminal holds
commands.desc: THE DOX VIEWER (src/js/dms.js, the DOX VIEWER button on the tool bar). A read-only DMS over the store: LIST what is there, SEARCH it by words and by the sense of the words, OPEN a document, READ a section, HEAD the top of one, OUTLINE its headings, FIND a string inside it (grep), INFO what it is, RELATE it to what else is about the same thing, STAT the totals, SCOPE which collections are read, INDEX the meaning lane, RELOAD the store from its sources. THE STORE IS FOUR COLLECTIONS: MEMORY is the LOREPACK (her memory - 76 MB, so the index reads the first 12 KB of each document and a document is read whole when it is opened), MANUAL is the manual's pages, DOCS is the shipped prose (README 477 KB, TODO, the chronicle, the packs), DATA the shipped json, and CODE the source itself - NOT part of ALL, because 2 MB of javascript is not a document; SHIPPED means every file under src/. THE TWO LANES: words are matched with BM25 over the fragments, each word STEMMED (saving = save) and EXPANDED through a table of the terminal's own vocabulary (CONCEPTS in src/js/dms.js: picture = image = render = photo = sprite) - that is what basic semantic search means with no key held; the MEANING lane is the embedding store (src/js/embed.js, namespace `docs`), built on purpose with /docs index because it costs one key call per fragment, and a search merges the two rankings with reciprocal rank fusion exactly as recall does. EVERY OPERATION IS A READ: this command and the panel both go through one store with no write, rename, move or delete in it - the only modules that change a document are the ones that own it (lore.js for her memory, rtfm-edit.js for a manual page, his editor for the source). A quoted phrase ("write the backup out") is looked for exactly and is not spread over the concepts beside it. THE READER'S ROW IS FIVE KEYS AND FOUR WAYS OF LOOKING AT ONE DOCUMENT (Patrikios, 2026-09-30: "The new button order should be THE STORE, TEXT, SUMMARY, OUTLINE, FIND, RELATED, EXPORT ... TEXT: Displays the text of the document only ... OUTLINE: Display the tags/keyword blocks only, (no doc text) ... GRAPH: New button. If exists, display simple GRAPH data in the LOREPACK for relationship, connections, etc."): ← THE STORE, TEXT, SUMMARY, OUTLINE, GRAPH, FIND, RELATED, EXPORT - the lit key says which page is on, a document always opens in TEXT (the text, the find bar and the foot, and nothing else), OUTLINE is the document's own tags and keywords, what the store's index says it is about, and every heading as a line you can press - with NO document text on it - and SUMMARY and GRAPH are their own pages. GRAPH sits after OUTLINE because the four are the same kind of thing (four ways of looking at the one document) while FIND, RELATED and EXPORT are things done with it. THE SUMMARY PAGE (kv `dms_summaries`, one record per document, keyed by the document, holding the text and the time it was made): if a summary is kept it is shown with its stamp and what it was made from; if none is kept the page ASKS before spending the call (one call to the text engine, the head of the document and the tail of a long one) and says what it would be made from; and leaving the page with a new one unsaved asks SAVE THIS SUMMARY BEFORE LEAVING? (SAVE IT / DISCARD IT / STAY HERE) wherever the way out is - another page, another document, the x, or /docs close. The document is never written to and nothing is uploaded: a summary lives BESIDE the document, on this device, which is what lets /docs summary <DOC> forget be an honest undo. THE GRAPH PAGE reads the LOREPACK's own triplet graph (the source / relation / object rows an imported MYTHOS pack was minted with, read whole through mythos.js): the relation inventory, a row per locus with its edges and fragments and the packs it came from, and a picture - sources in one column, objects in the other, ordered so the curves cross as little as they can, capped at twelve names a side and drawn with a numbered disc on each curve that the numbered edge list below is the key to. With a document open it is that document's own share of the graph (its top terms and title words, matched at word starts so "he" cannot match "the"), and with no document open it is a sample of the whole of it. THE TWO LONG TEXT LISTS ARE PAGINATED (Patrikios, 2026-09-30: "Paginate DOX VIEWER MAIN STAGE text results"): the store list and the search results are drawn A PAGE AT A TIME - NINE ROWS, a page that FITS the stage and no more (2026-09-30: "limit pagination to 9 max as this is what fills the MAIN STAGE at my current font size and looks good") - and the paginator is a CONTROL DECK of its own at the foot of the page, directly above the chat block (2026-09-30: "make the paginator graphic with simple buttons in a control deck at the bottom of the page above the chat block") - the graphic is a row of numbered PAGE CHIPS with the page you are on inverted, the first and the last always drawn and the runs between them elided as "...", the simple buttons are the arrow keys either side of them with FIRST and LAST at the outer ends, and PAGE n OF m / SHOWING a-b OF t is printed beside the lot - so a store of a thousand documents and a search of sixty hits are not one scroll to fish in, and the way to the next page is never scrolled away. The page never changes the answer: every row is still drawn, nine to a page. The same page is printed in the LOG - `/docs list [SCOPE] PAGE 3`, `/docs search <WORDS> [SCOPE] PAGE 2`, `/docs find <TEXT> PAGE 2` (a bare number after list is a page too: `/docs list 3`) - and LIA_DMS_PAGE in src/js/config.js moves the size. The reader's own window is NOT this pager: a page of a document is a screenful of LINES (260), a page of a list is a screenful of ROWS. FILL THE STAGE (the button in its bar, or /docs full) gives the viewer the WHOLE page: the upper deck's status line and tool bar and the lower deck both stand down for it, the conversation waits underneath, and Esc, /docs full off or the x gives the stage back. FILLING THE STAGE IS THE DEFAULT (Patrikios, 2026-09-26: "DOX VIEWER when selected overlays everything, the MAIN STAGE is in FOCUS. All CONTROL DECKS are COLLAPSED", and 2026-09-30: "In DOX VIEWER make FILL THE STAGE default"), so the FILL key is not a hidden extra - it is what the panel does. Selecting the viewer gives it the whole stage; giving the stage back by hand is quiet only for the REST OF THAT SESSION (nothing is written down), so the next load fills again, because the default is the default. THE TANDEM: the viewer is the one page the two of them look at TOGETHER. HITL is him - his eye is wherever the reader's window is, and he points at a line by pressing it. ALIA is her (the Autonomous Liminal Intelligence Agent, src/js/config.js): she is told what is on the stage and where he is reading on every turn it is open, with the lines he can see quoted, and her hand turns the page - a PAGE line in a reply opens the document at a line on his screen, marked as hers, which is /docs look <DOC> @ <LINE> from his side. /docs tandem [on|off] is the shared page itself. And talking does not stop for any of it: the panel's own foot carries the talk strip - both presences, the newest line of the log, LIVE / TALK / LISTEN, and a one-line box that drives the same input and the same send the lower deck's box does - because a viewer puts the lower deck down, and a page that has to be closed in order to speak is not a page the two of them can share.

commands.short: THE SHARED PAGE - whether ALIA sees what you are reading, and whether she can turn it
commands.desc: THE SHARED PAGE (src/js/dms.js, THE TANDEM; the DOX VIEWER is the thing it is about). Two sides of the same coin: HITL is Patrikios - the human in the loop, whose eye is wherever the reader's window is and who points at a line by pressing it; ALIA is her - the Autonomous Liminal Intelligence Agent, who is told what is on the stage and where he is reading on every turn the viewer is open, and whose hand can TURN THE PAGE under his eyes (a PAGE line in a reply, or /docs look from his side). Bare or `state`, it names both presences and what each is pointed at; `off` stops the block being sent to her and refuses her page turns (said plainly, never quietly dropped); `on` hands the page back to her. The window, his pointed-at line and hers are what she is told - never a document she cannot see. Nothing in it can write: the only thing either of them can move is the other's attention.

commands.usage: /screen [look <ID|#TAG|WORDS> | next | prev | take | tandem on|off | status]
commands.short: THE SCREENING ROOM - the full stage as the page you both look at together
commands.desc: THE SCREENING ROOM (src/js/images.js, THE SCREENING TANDEM; the full stage / lightbox is the thing it is about). Two sides of the same coin: HITL is Patrikios - the human in the loop, whose eye is on the open record and who walks it with the arrows; ALIA is her - told what record is on the stage on every turn it is open (what it was made from, what she read in it, her take filed on it) and whose hand can TURN THE STAGE under his eyes (a STAGE line in a reply, or /screen look from his side). Bare or `status`, it names the open record and both presences; `tandem off` stops the screening block being sent to her and refuses her stage turns (said plainly, never quietly dropped); `tandem on` hands the stage back to her. `look` turns it, `next`/`prev` walk it, `take` reads the open picture in her critical voice (HER TAKE, one vision call, pictures only). Nothing on it can write: the only thing either of them can move is the other's attention.

commands.short: put ONE document in front of her, by decision rather than recall
commands.desc: SEE - ONE DOCUMENT PUT IN FRONT OF HER. Canon is what she always has and recall is a guess at what matches the question; this is a DECISION: one document out of the LOREPACK, read out of the store and handed to her whole with your next message, as what she is looking at. A name (or words from one) puts it there, `clear` takes it out, bare it says what is in focus. One at a time, spent once she has answered, bounded by LIA_FOCUS_CHARS (a bigger scroll is handed up to there, and both sides are told the rest was not) - or name `part N` to hand her one numbered passage of a big scroll instead (the original stays whole; parts are reads, and she is told which part of how many she is looking at, so asking him to turn the page is ordinary). The SEE button in the DOCS panel is the same door with a click, and the name of what is in focus is shown on the lorebar

commands.short: the agent of the record, with hands
commands.desc: ARCHIVAX - THE AGENT OF THE RECORD, WITH HANDS. Order 0 of the agent manifest (src/mythos/agents.json): the keeper of memory, commitment and revision history, and the only agent here that acts instead of speaking. Bare, /archivax reports the record as she sees it (pictures, how many have a reading, the tags, the folders) and her journal; `ops` lists what she may be told to do - file pictures into folders, tag them, untag them, read them, classify them (read + tag), and sweep the newest unread ones into the record; `journal` prints everything she has done, oldest last. SHE TAKES DIRECTION FROM EITHER SIDE OF THE GLASS: from Patrikios here, and from a LIA with one [[ARCHIVAX: <OP> ...]] line in her reply. From a LIA, the glass holds: she may be set only on what the TERMINAL MADE (a render, an upscale), never on what Patrikios handed over himself - he may order anything. She never deletes, never runs code, and every op she runs is written into her journal and into that turn's archive entry. /help archivax goes deeper

commands.usage: /backup [status | diag | kept | snapshot | pull | autosave on|off|now | help]
commands.short: the generator's own source, zipped out of this page
commands.desc: THE GENERATOR'S OWN SOURCE, DOWNLOADED FROM THIS PAGE, AND KEPT ON THIS DEVICE. Bare, it builds a zip of everything - main.pjs, index.html and every file under src/, read out of the running terminal right now, including files the server has never been given - and hands it to this machine's Downloads folder; nothing is uploaded and nothing is changed. `status` answers the other half of the question: which source files are on the SERVER and which have never been saved. That matters because this page is served its unsaved files locally, so a partial save is invisible here and fatal everywhere else - a phone, a tablet, the public URL gets 404s for those files and the terminal cannot start at all. `diag` reports what the device can and cannot do (iOS version, file storage, microphone, download support) for a device where the terminal will not start. AUTOSAVE is the answer to a page you are afraid to leave: on every boot where the build is COHERENT (the scripts this page loaded are exactly the scripts the packed copy of index.html names) AND the source is not all on the server yet, the whole tree is zipped and kept ON THIS DEVICE in kv - newest snapshot only - so the work survives a closed tab even if the save never fired. `kept` prints that snapshot (when, how many files, how big), `pull` downloads it, `snapshot` forces one now, `autosave off|on` disarms or arms it. THE PAGE CANNOT PRESS SAVE: the editor lives on another origin, so autosave is insurance, not a save. A BACKUP IS NOT A SAVE: only the editor's save button puts the work on the server

commands.short: the save check - is the work saved? the server's copy against this workspace, file for file
commands.desc: THE SAVE CHECK - "IS THE WORK SAVED?" ASKED OF THE PLATFORM, BECAUSE ONLY THE EDITOR'S SAVE BUTTON PUBLISHES THIS GENERATOR AND THIS PAGE CANNOT PRESS IT. It reads the copy the server is holding RIGHT NOW (perchance.org/api/downloadGenerator, through the relay - their API sends no CORS headers, so the page's own fetch is refused) and compares it against this workspace: main.pjs and index.html BYTE FOR BYTE (with the first line that differs when one does), the file list, EVERY src/ FILE BY CONTENT, and the import lines. It is the only thing here that compares CONTENTS: /backup status names which files the server has never been given, but the page it reads that manifest out of is itself the SERVED copy (measured: an unsaved probe in main.pjs did not move it), so only a fresh read of the server can see a changed file - and each saved file's manifest key is also its name on the platform's own CDN (user.uploads.dev/file/<key>), so it is read back and compared byte for byte rather than by size, which catches a one-character edit. 127 files take about half a second. WHAT IT IS NOT: it writes nothing, uploads nothing, reads no key, changes nothing, and nothing in the terminal waits on it. A BACKUP IS NOT A SAVE - /backup TAKES A COPY, SAVE PUBLISHES IT, /saved PROVES IT LANDED. It says nothing about the conversation: the archive lives in this browser (kv) and is /sync's and /cloud's business. /help saved has the whole of it.

commands.usage: /sync [status | versions | pick | connect | up | down [NAME] | forget | help]
commands.short: the conversation out of this browser, and back - the chat backups on your own drive
commands.desc: THE CONVERSATION ITSELF, OUT OF THIS BROWSER AND BACK. There are two backups in this terminal and they answer two different fears. /backup carries the GENERATOR'S SOURCE - the code - and not one word of the conversation. The archive (kv: sacred_archive / master_log, the newest 1000 turns) is the other thing, and it lives in THIS BROWSER and nowhere else: PURGE, a cleared profile or a new machine takes every word of it. This is the door onto the CHAT BACKUPS kept on his own drive (G:). Bare, `status`: which folder is connected or in hand, this device's own name (stamped into every backup it writes), how many turns the archive holds here and when the newest one is, and the last runs. `versions` lists every backup in the folder, newest first, with its turns, its date and its size. PICK asks for the folder: this terminal reads it, lists the versions in it and TAKES THE NEWEST ONE IN on its own - looking changes nothing, nothing is written to the folder and nothing is uploaded. DROP does the same with a folder dragged onto the panel. `up` writes the archive out as lia-terminal-archive.json - into the connected folder, or to this machine's Downloads folder when there is none - plus ONE DATED VERSION A DAY beside it in a connected folder, so the folder accumulates VERSIONS rather than only the latest state. `down [NAME|newest]` takes one backup in. THE MERGE ONLY ADDS, and that is the whole safety of it: a turn this device does not have at all comes in, and a turn it already holds is KEPT EXACTLY AS IT IS - the backup may only FILL what is missing on it (her half if it is empty here, her stamp, his words, a ref it does not carry) and never overwrites one that is there. The archive's own 1000-turn cap is applied last, with a warning if it bites, and nothing is ever deleted. TWO SHAPES ARE READ: the terminal's own backup (exact - every turn verbatim, and written here) and the readable export the EXPORT button writes, archive_<digits>.txt (his words, her words, the stamps, the layer, the media refs and her own lanes come back; a render's recipe is prose there, so its creation lines are COUNTED in the receipt rather than faked). WHERE IT CAN REACH, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: the File System Access folder picker is REFUSED inside the editor's frame ('Cross origin sub frames aren't allowed to show a file picker'), so from the preview it is PICK (a directory input) and DROP, and what leaves goes out through the browser's own download; on a TOP-LEVEL tab the picker IS allowed, and then CONNECT keeps the folder and `up` writes straight into it, the handle remembered on this device. THE PANEL is SYNC in the upper deck: press it, press PICK, choose the folder - or drop the folder on the panel. THE SAME PANEL CARRIES A SECOND ROAD, and /cloud is it: a single file in his own Google Drive, for the OTHER DEVICE.

commands.usage: /local [status | test | models | model [id] | base [url] | chat <text> | see [question]]
commands.short: local model lane - LM Studio, Atomic Cat, anything OpenAI-compatible, no key
commands.desc: LOCAL (src/js/local.js - the uncensored road; OpenAI-compatible /v1, no key, direct browser call). `status` says whether the server answers and what is set. `models` lists what the server holds right now. `model [id]` names the model she sends with. `base [url]` points at another server (default his LM Studio). `chat <text>` is one shot through the set model - the lane proving itself, not her voice. `see [question]` picks a picture or clip and shows it to the set model - a clip goes as 4 stills down the same sampleFrames road her eyes use (needs a vision-capable model). HTTPS-PAGE LIMIT, STATED IN THE LANE: this page is served over https and browsers refuse plain-http LAN calls, so an http-only server on the LAN is unreachable from here - the lane works the moment the endpoint is https-reachable (tunnel, or any hosted OpenAI-compatible server).

commands.short: chatlogs out of this browser onto his own Mythos server
commands.desc: BRIDGE (src/js/bridge.js + src/server/mythos-chatlog-server.mjs - the conversation out of this browser's IndexedDB and onto the machine that is always on, one append-only JSONL file per agent). The server runs on his machine: node src/server/mythos-chatlog-server.mjs [port] (default 8098, zero dependencies, MYTHOS_BRIDGE_KEY locks it). `status` says whether the store answers, turns here and turns there. `push` sends every turn the store is missing (the store dedupes by stamp, so pushing twice changes nothing). `pull` takes every turn this browser is missing (the merge only adds by stamp - nothing here is overwritten). `base [url]` points at the store, `key [k]` is its key when locked (never printed), `agent [id]` is whose file the turns go to (default LIA). Same HTTPS-PAGE LIMIT as /local: an http-only LAN server is unreachable from the served page - run it from a locally-served copy or over a tunnel.

commands.short: Groq chat lane - the fastest brain, key held in the keyring
commands.desc: GROQ (src/js/groq.js - the MODELS lane; key in the KEYRING panel under Groq, never pasted here). OpenAI-compatible chat, direct from this browser - no relay. Bare, or `status`: whether the key proves alive and which model is in force. `test` probes the key. `models` lists every chat model on the account, live, with the set one starred. `model [id]` names the model she sends with. `chat <text>` is one shot through the set model - the lane proving itself, not her voice.

commands.short: the portable per-agent record - one pack per agent, importable, loadable into the lorepack
commands.desc: COMMPACK (src/commpack/commpack.js - the shared recorder module, one implementation for both homes; spec src/commpack/COMMPACK.SPEC.md; lane src/js/commpack.js). ONE PACK PER AGENT, max 15, IDs minted once (HITL-001, SIA-002 through SIA-015, ARCHIVAX) - identity binds the Actor, never the RoleLayer. The pack lives in THIS BROWSER (localStorage commpack_*, append-only JSONL: header line, turns, params-version events) and NOT ONE WORD OF IT is in src/, which is public. Bare, or `status [AGENT]`: turns, chars, params version and fingerprint per pack held here. `export <AGENT> [md]` writes the pack out as .jsonl (md adds the readable Lane-1 document). `import <AGENT>` picks a .jsonl and seam-appends it - duplicates skipped, both fingerprint shapes accepted, human/agent roles normalized on the way in. `lore <AGENT>` is LANE 1: the pack's readable document loaded into the LOREPACK (private kv, this browser only - src/lorepack/ stays untouched). Lane 2 (factory staging) is the .jsonl itself, which stages straight into the factory.

commands.short: the whole conversation out as a file - readable, or full-fidelity
commands.desc: THE CONVERSATION OUT OF THIS BROWSER, AS A FILE. Bare (or the EXPORT button in the deck) it writes the READABLE one: a .txt with every turn in order, each carrying its own stamp, ROLE, HITL and LIA ID lines, the images and clips it holds by their vault name, what she looked at and asked to see again, her own lanes (kept, let go, wanted, released) and every creation with its whole recipe - the file to read, to print, or to hand to someone. json writes the OTHER one: lia-terminal-archive.json, the archive's own entries exactly as they are kept - stamps, roles, edits, vault references and all - the ROUND-TRIP file, which IMPORT reads back whole. IMPORT (the deck button, beside EXPORT) takes either one back in: the .json whole, or the .txt best-effort (his words, her words, the layers and the stamps survive; a picture stays named by the vault id it had HERE, so it shows where this device still holds it). THE MERGE ONLY ADDS: a turn already here is SKIPPED by its stamp, so importing the same file twice duplicates nothing, and importing a backup from another device brings in the turns this one is missing. /sync and /cloud do the same pair of jobs with a folder or a Drive at the far end.

commands.usage: /cloud [status | setup | connect | send | receive | log | forget]
commands.short: the conversation to your own Google Drive, and back - the other device's road
commands.desc: THE CONVERSATION TO YOUR OWN GOOGLE DRIVE AND BACK - the cloud road of THE SYNC, and the answer to the one thing the folder road cannot do: a folder on THIS disk is invisible to a phone or a laptop, and a Drive is not. ONE FILE is involved, lia-terminal-archive.json - the same full-fidelity document /export json writes - created once by SEND and updated by every SEND after, read back by RECEIVE through the importer (merged by stamp, nothing duplicated). SETUP IS HIS, ONCE, IN HIS OWN GOOGLE CLOUD CONSOLE (nothing of ours is involved): setup prints the whole recipe - new project, enable the Drive API, add yourself as a test user, create a WEB OAuth client, register the exact REDIRECT URL the panel shows (COPY takes it), paste the CLIENT ID into the panel and press CONNECT, then approve in the popup. THE CLIENT ID IS A PUBLIC IDENTIFIER, not a secret, and is kept on this device (kv: lia_settings / sync_cloud); THE TOKENS ARE SECRETS and live only in the key ring, under "google-drive" - never printed, never in the transcript, never in the archive, never handed to her (the key ring scrubs every error before it is shown). SCOPE IS drive.file: THE TERMINAL CAN ONLY EVER TOUCH THE ONE FILE IT CREATED ITSELF - it cannot list, read or change anything else in the Drive. log prints the run record kept on this device: when, which direction, how many bytes, and whether it worked - stamps and counts, never a word of the conversation. forget (twice, or forget yes) drops the tokens from this browser and leaves the cloud file alone. THE PANEL is the SYNC button in the upper deck: the folder road is at the top of it and this road sits under.

commands.usage: /ldrive [status | open | pull | push [/FOLDER|all] | auto [on|off] | forget | help]
commands.short: a folder on your own disk, read and written in place - the drive window road
commands.desc: THE DRIVE ROAD (src/js/drive.js + src/drive.html) - a folder on his own disk, read AND written in place, which neither of the other roads in the SYNC panel can do: the folder road (/sync) can only take in, and the cloud road (/cloud) reaches a Drive, not a disk. The frame this terminal is served in refuses the folder picker, so the drive lives in its own window - /ldrive open opens it (allow pop-ups), and the folder is linked THERE, where the picker is allowed: a mapped drive, an external disk, a photo library. /ldrive pull brings the linked folder's pictures into the vault (kind attach, folder /images, tagged drive - only what is new, name and size). /ldrive push [/FOLDER] saves one vault folder's pictures (default /images) onto the drive, into a Mythos subfolder - never over the folder's own files, and nothing pulled is ever pushed back. Pictures only, both ways. Chrome and Edge have the folder picker; elsewhere the road says so and stands down. Nothing is ever uploaded anywhere.

commands.short: voice control of the console - spoken orders that work the switches
commands.desc: VOICE CONTROL (src/js/voxcont.js) - VOXCONTPACK'S HANDS. WHEN ARMED (/voxcont on, or the VOICE CONTROL button in the pilot's seat), words spoken on the LIACOMM key work the console instead of going to her: name a switch and it moves (GALLERY, STAGE, FRAME, CENTER, VIMEO, BACKSTAGE, SHIFT, SHELF, SCRIPTS, KEYS, MOOD, SYSTEM, TOOLS, CHATLOG, SYNC, DRIVE, DOCS, DRAFT, VOICES - OPEN or CLOSE before it, or CLOSE IT for the one open panel), PULL THE DRIVE, MIRROR THE VAULT (ASKED FIRST - SAY YES WITHIN 2 MINUTES, YES/NO ANSWERS A PENDING ORDER), PICS, FONT BIGGER or SMALLER, UPPER/LOWER/LEFT/RIGHT DECK on|off, LISTEN (say again), SEND IT, STOP (always works, even OFF). Anything else on the key goes to her as chat. VOICE IS INPUT, NOT AUTHORITY: renders, upscales, strikes, deletes and wipes never ride voice - those need his hand. /voxcont say <WORDS> tries one command from text with no microphone. LIFTED FROM the mythos-designer VOXCONTPACK (src/agent/voxcontpack-inventory.md, ferry chip src/chips/vox-controller-chip/voiceDomController.ts): its normalize/find/click/adjust machinery re-cut for this console, its designer tabs and themes left behind.

commands.usage: /theme [status | list | crt | import <JSON> | url <URL> | export [crt] | forget | help]
